notes: com.amazonaws.<region>.<service> names the service an endpoint fronts. Resolving it is what draws 'this VPC reaches S3 privately' - without it the private path stops at the endpoint and the reader cannot tell what it connects to.
An alias record points at a load balancer by DNS name, never by id. Pure value equality is the only join available.
Alias records to a CloudFront distribution match on its domain name.
A CNAME holding a load balancer's DNS name. Weaker than an alias because the value is free text and may point outside the account.
Target group back to its load balancer. An ARN join rather than a name join, so it is exact.
Registered targets are instance ids when TargetType is instance, and raw IPs when it is ip - the value's shape decides which.
A rule CIDR that contains or overlaps a subnet's CIDR. Containment, not equality, and 0.0.0.0/0 must be treated as the internet rather than as matching every subnet.
0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 marks a default route. Not a join to another resource - it qualifies the route's gateway edge, and is the single value that decides public versus private.
An S3 origin's domain embeds the bucket name (<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com), so the bucket must be parsed out before matching.
A custom origin pointing at a load balancer.
